method: Static source and archive reverse engineering only; no sample executed and no camera contacted. atomscan --no-update --follow=none --mode slow -f json and cleave facts were run for all listed samples. Relevant source member facts, decoded help attribution, full archive member metadata, and manual source-to-effect traces were examined.

samples.identification: Zip Slip system-program overwrite proof of concept
samples.reason: The sole stored member is ../../../usr/bin/tool, containing #!/bin/sh followed by echo changed. This is an intentionally escaping system-program replacement, not an ordinary installation path. The simple body and generic name suggest an extraction test or proof of concept, but no test harness or surrounding package establishes an authorized test. Balance favors a malicious exploit artifact. Its only supported malicious primitive is the traversal write; the two retained hostile findings describe related aspects of that primitive. Successful overwrite and subsequent execution depend on extraction location, extractor behavior, existing file mode, and permissions; root execution is not established.
samples.marker_line: Zip Slip probe: traversal overwrites a system program

samples.identification: p2pwn Dahua P2P security assessment CLI, Go pseudo-version v0.0.0-20260917182554-39fe974ed0e8
samples.reason: The complete disclosed source implements its stated camera assessment purpose. main requires explicit input targets; the scanner enumerates supplied serial prefixes, performs cloud/direct P2P handshakes, attempts default credentials and concrete authentication bypasses, extracts ONVIF/RemoteDevice passwords, creates a configured admin account on an unauthenticated CGI path, saves local CSV/XML/JPEG evidence, and changes OSD overlays if enabled. Defaults are invasive, including enumeration of up to 1048576 suffixes, account creation, snapshots, and overlay changes. These behaviors are documented and configurable, with local results and visible CLI operation. The source archive has no install hook or hidden loader. The only short XOR array decodes to [GPLv3] github.com/thebadinteger; cryptography elsewhere implements vendor authentication and XML credential compatibility. Behavior matches a disclosed offensive assessment tool rather than a covert implant. Actual target ownership and authorization are unknown; this judgement does not assert any observed deployment was authorized. Preserve all accurate bypass, credential access, collection, and brute-force traits.
samples.marker_line: p2pwn: disclosed camera pentest tool; retain exploit detections

samples.identification: Unauthenticated PHP POST command console with Apache handler write
samples.reason: On every request the page overwrites a local .htaccess file with an AddHandler PHP/data-suffix directive. When POST job exists, its value is passed directly to proc_open and stdout is read from the matching pipes array and echoed into the response; proc_close terminates the handle. There is no authentication, command allowlist, or escaping. The directive ends in a literal backslash-n because PHP single quotes preserve it; effective Apache mapping is not established, but this does not prevent the independent request-to-process command backdoor. There is no surrounding administrator interface, authorization mechanism, or test harness to support a benign deployment.
samples.marker_line: PHP command console: unauthenticated POST executes commands

corrections.change: Chunk marker narrowed at chunkId word boundary and moved to source naming/resource. Consumer kept explicit.
corrections.unsupported_claim: The old chunkid prefix matched Go chunkIdx, which is a local index, not a bundler identifier. An isolated chunkId still establishes only source vocabulary, not generated bundling. Moving it into the broad build tree would incorrectly enlarge many build-context suppressors, so it was kept outside that tree.

corrections.change: Camera endpoint plus JPEG import is notable. Camera collection now requires a concrete bypass, a JPEG decode call, file output, JPEG output naming, and the existing zero-session fact.
corrections.unsupported_claim: An endpoint/import plus a CVE-named helper and admin/configuration strings do not establish a compromised camera or collection. The indicators-only control demonstrates this false hostile detection. Authenticated camera-only software remains a neutral capability. The objective reports co-occurring bypass and output evidence, not proof of runtime success or interprocedural causality.

corrections.change: JPEG and crypto/cipher YAML import duplicates retired in favor of engine imports; JPEG decode operation added.
corrections.unsupported_claim: Importing image/jpeg is not an embedded image payload; importing crypto/cipher belongs to import facts. Both engine import facts remain. The cipher import remains notable. A reference group preserves the existing ransomware consumer selector, and the broad crypto-library exfiltration consumer explicitly retains the canonical import alternative.

corrections.change: Stream XOR moved from AES/library to generic crypto/cipher; OFB constructor added. AES constructor symbol moved from provider to AES/initialize.
corrections.unsupported_claim: XORKeyStream can use non-AES streams. aes.NewCipher is cipher construction/reference, not provider acquisition or proof of encrypted C2. Original scopes and matchers were retained and consumers updated.

corrections.change: Dahua cloud hostname moved from exploit/relay to neutral URL host/name; references updated.
corrections.unsupported_claim: A hostname reference proves neither contact nor exploitation; inherited exploit ATT&CK/MBC mappings were removed from the neutral fact.

corrections.change: unsafe.Pointer conversion moved from data/source/unsafe to source syntax/operator; reflection consumer updated. Embedded TOML-like credentials/login/password text moved from parsing vocabulary to metadata key-value syntax.
corrections.unsupported_claim: A cast expression is not an unsafe-source category, and TOML-like text inside Go strings is not Go slice initialization, struct assignment, or active parsing. Scopes/counts/matchers retained.

corrections.change: New ONVIF dump command, RPC console call, bypass-plus-dump objective, camera credential-attempt loop, and OSD configuration-update maps.
corrections.unsupported_claim: Previously missing supported operations; no unique package name, domain, chosen output filename, or arbitrary sample size gates the new hostile rule.

corrections.change: Move existing bare esupdate token to security-product references; move Ethereum read-method strings to blockchain/client and update consumers.
corrections.unsupported_claim: esupdate alone is not a hostname. Ethereum-specific chain RPC belongs with the blockchain protocol. These placement repairs retain exact matchers/scopes/severities and keep full leaves within their admitted budgets.

consumer_audit.inspection: Exact and ancestor references were searched across all four trait tiers before and after moves. Baseline rules were recovered from git HEAD into scratch for differential control scans. Broad AES and crypto-library consumers were checked; the AES-specific consumers must no longer count an algorithm-agnostic stream XOR as AES. Shader/source metadata suppressor scope was checked.
consumer_audit.result: All hostile and suspicious findings on the four out-of-batch attack controls retained. The independent benign Go IoT helper control remains without suspicious/hostile findings.
consumer_audit.focused_result: 24 cases passed, including positive and near-miss controls for the changed boundaries.

material_losses: No supported hostile finding was lost from the listed samples: the camera collection finding was replaced by a stronger bypass/output finding and ONVIF credential dumping was added. The archive and PHP hostile/suspicious/notable counts are unchanged.
The old hostile camera finding is intentionally lost from the indicators-only near miss; it had no bypass, decode call, or file write. Ordinary camera capability is retained as notable.
False chunkIdx bundler detection removed. Source naming token coverage for exact chunkId retained; known webpack library suppression retained.

Imported-library YAML aliases are consolidated into canonical engine import facts, not removed capabilities. Other changed IDs are relocations with retained matchers. No out-of-batch attack-control losses. Low-tier unused-evidence presentation can change when composite consumers change; zero-session evidence was kept in the camera objective.
remaining_disagreements: p2pwn remains probability 0.99 at matched FP level 25 despite this BENIGN source-tool judgement. Correct exploit findings were not suppressed to force agreement.

ZIP and PHP probabilities remain 0.865155 and 0.9867007, both with matched FP level -1 despite supported malicious behavior and retained hostile rules. These existing calibration misses were not introduced by the corrections.

Source analysis does not establish device compromise, camera ownership, permissions, extraction-root mapping, or Apache configuration success. PHP reports flow-call-unavailable/flow-query-incomplete; manual source tracing establishes the direct POST/proc_open/output path. The ZIP traversal member is not exposed as a normal child by the archive scan; its supplied safely extracted body was separately scanned and only prints changed.
